PARA:
Radar Cruise Control System Control
The control performed by the radar cruise control system differs depending on the selected control mode (vehicle-to-vehicle distance control mode or constant speed control mode).
Vehicle-to-vehicle Distance Control Mode A mode in which the system recognizes and judges the driving lanes of the preceding vehicle and own vehicle, and follows the preceding vehicle while maintaining an appropriate vehicle-to-vehicle distance according to vehicle speed.
Constant Speed Control Mode A mode in which the vehicle speed is kept constant according to the set vehicle speed.
Glossary
Low Speed Limit The lower limit speed of the controllable range. It is set to approximately 40km/h.
Minimum Set Vehicle Speed The lower limit speed of the settable range. It is distinguished from the low speed limit. It is set to approximately 50km/h.
High Speed Limit (Constant speed control mode only) The upper limit speed of the controllable range. It is set to approximately 100km/h.
Maximum Set Vehicle Speed The upper limit speed of the settable range. It is set to approximately 100km/h.
